name: TabLit
description: TabLit: A Demographic-Aware Benchmark for Modeling Early Literacy Outcomes (NeurIPS, under review). TabLit is a single-table tabular benchmark for early reading risk and longitudinal recovery prediction, covering two student cohorts from a single U.S. metropolitan-area research site. The 'cohort' column identifies which cohort each student belongs to: D2 (2) = a Kindergarten Fall + End-of-Year cohort (n=1,039); D4 (4) = a G1->G4 longitudinal panel (n=318). The two cohorts were administered different assessment batteries by design, so columns specific to a given cohort's battery are populated only for that cohort's rows; users should mask, not impute, those structurally-empty cells.
citeAs: Anonymous Author. TabLit: A Demographic-Aware Benchmark for Modeling Early Literacy Outcomes. NeurIPS, under review.
rai:dataLimitations: D2: single-site U.S. metropolitan-area Kindergarten cohort (n=1,039); demographic fields come from a voluntary parent survey with 47-50% non-response; the Fall cognitive battery follows a non-overlapping sub-sample design (204 received all three subtests, 312 received one subtest only, 523 received none). End-of-Year follow-up coverage: NWD 49.6%, LWR 49.5%, CELF-5 SC 19.7%, CELF-5 RS 47.0%. D4: single-site G1->G4 panel with grade-to-grade attrition (n=318 -> 298 -> 285 -> 220); per-grade mean column missingness rises from 3.9% (G1) to 36.5% (G4); per-form Word-Use Repertoire and SAT-10 percentile have lower coverage even within completed grades. The two cohorts were administered different assessment batteries, so columns specific to a given cohort's battery are NaN on rows from the other cohort by construction; this is structural missingness and should be masked, not modeled as MCAR/MAR.
rai:dataBiases: D2: single-site enrolment; race composition (per voluntary parent survey): white 28.6%, black 15.4%, multi-racial 5.8%, hispanic 4.9%, asian 1.4%; ~48% missing demographic data; cognitive battery administered only in cohort year 1 (correlated with year). D4: single-site enrolment cohort entering G1 in 2007-08; race composition: white 59.4%, black 24.5%, mixed/multiple 6.0%, hispanic 4.4%, asian 3.8%; sex 51.3% male / 48.1% female. Demographic balance is fixed at intake and does not vary across grades.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Both cohorts ship de-identified student-level records: no names, dates of birth, school identifiers, or direct identifiers. D2 demographics are voluntary parent-survey responses (gender, ethnicity, race, language). D4 carries only Sex and Race at G1 intake.
rai:dataUseCases: Early-reading risk prediction (D2 static at-risk indicator); longitudinal reading-recovery prediction (D4 G1 -> G3 spelling-score crossing); tabular ML benchmarking under structured (MNAR) sub-battery and longitudinal-attrition missingness; cross-cohort generalization studies.
rai:dataSocialImpact: All cohorts released under CC BY 4.0; re-use permitted with attribution. Neither cohort is appropriate for individual student diagnostic or placement decisions.
prov:wasDerivedFrom: Cohort 2: Kindergarten Fall battery and end-of-year follow-up assessments at a single U.S. metropolitan-area research site. Cohort 4: Single-site G1->G4 longitudinal study at the same research site.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: TabLit.csv contains all per-student records from both cohorts, with a 'cohort' column (2 or 4) identifying each row's cohort. Cohort 2 records carry 2 derived binary at-risk indicator columns (ktea3_nwd_target, ktea3_lwr_target) thresholded at standard score < 90; cohort 4 records carry 1 derived binary recovery target column (crossed_spell_target) thresholded on a G1 -> G3 spelling standard-score crossing of 100. Columns specific to one cohort's assessment battery are NaN on rows from the other cohort. TabLit_raw.csv is built identically but without the derived target columns.
